chapter: Bass, drums and the big-band rhythm section
title: Walter Page, Basie and Freddie Green: keeping out of each other's way
summary: Page's balance ideas, one piano in Moten's band, Freddie Green's single chords and why bop dropped the guitar.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Well, I mean Fletcher had Kaiser tried to
Yeah, well, I mean to say, it was more like bang-bang-bang, if you can understand what I mean.
Yes.

Instead of you hearing a solid teamwork. Now this is where I say Walter Page came in. After those bands, you heard Earl Hines in his early days. He had all the beautiful arrangements, and he sounded so beautiful on the piano. He had a good rhythm section, but he wasn't even.
No, not until he got up to Alvin Bowers (phonetic); then it was good.
Yeah.
Yeah, that's right.

And so, now Page'll sit down and tell the guys, "Now listen, we gotta' get the balance." And the next thing is, he said, "We gonna (either have to) get rid of the guitar or the piano; you gotta stay outa' the way." Now this was just right in Basie's lap, 'cause when they came to Texas, Basie with Benny Moten's band, they only had one piano. So, Moten would sit over there and play the bass part, and what's-her-name would play on that one piano, play the
treble, you know.
Uh-oh.
They learned how to stay out of each other's way there. There was no problem at all there for the Basie would stay out of the way of the guitar. Now if you'll notice--
That's a very interesting part point because what he was doing there was what he more-or-less does later when he gets rid of Page--
Yeah.
I see. That's very interesting.

Uh-huh. Yeah. Now if you'll notice in Basie's band, that famous guitarist, Freddie Green, does not flirt with the chords, if you understand what I mean. You know, chords can and follow progressions. Chords can stay just on the rudiments, and that way people know where you are, and they don't have to clash with you.
Yeah. Right.

And Freddie Green--why he's so great is all the music that he knows, he's got enough forte, I guess you'd say, to just play that one chord, the fundamental chord, that is. So, then he doesn't get in the way of the piano.
Right.
Now you notice when bop came in, they eliminated the guitar player.
Yeah, well, they--
Because he was clashing with the piano, you see.
Right.
The piano player may be going this way, and the guitar player might be going that way. They would clash.
Right.

So they had to get rid of one of them. And then when the amplified guitar came in, then not only did the piano have trouble with the guitar, but the bass player started to havin' trouble, 'cause that guy with that amplifier -- like I could speak of one guy -- (inaudible) I think the band broke up when I left.
